case_question: Removing a thing is neither final nor self-contained here. The removal path can run again on something already removed and does real work the second time instead of stopping, and the cleanup it triggers for the removed thing's stored derivatives is aimed by a name prefix rather than by identity - so it reaches every stored object whose name begins the same way, including ones belonging to entities that merely share a naming ancestor and were never meant to be touched. The two faults compound: a repeat removal re-runs a cascade that was already too wide. Elsewhere in the folder the same two obligations are met on purpose: one library routes every removal - single, batched, and clear-all - through one mutator so the terminal state is the same however you get there, another keeps a keyed family of entries where dropping one member is defined not to disturb its siblings, and another draws an explicit line between matching an entry by its exact identity and matching it by a partial leading fragment, because the second is a filter and must never be used where the first is meant. Which files make removal non-terminal and aim its cascade by prefix, and which own the terminal-and-scoped-removal contract they have to be brought in line with?

retriever.surface: Opus 5 with ONLY the graphify knowledge-graph MCP server: a single merged cross-repo graph. No Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, filesystem access, network, or subagents.
retriever.checkout_verified: run.sh gates on git rev-parse HEAD == pinned commit for all 15 repositories before launch
retriever.isolation: kernel-enforced by sandbox-exec with absolute subpaths: gold, the answer vault and every sibling arm are unreadable; no prior-run transcript is readable; fresh cwd; no settings sources loaded

cost.launch: fresh isolated `claude -p` under sandbox-exec, --setting-sources '' --disable-slash-commands, --strict-mcp-config with ONLY the shared graphify MCP server (one graph merged across the pinned repos), --allowedTools mcp__graphify__* and --disallowedTools Bash,Read,Write,Edit,Grep,Glob,...
cost.cache_prefix_only_note: The first-turn cache read is the CLI's static system-prompt and tool-definition prefix, which is byte-identical across sessions on this machine and was warm from unrelated earlier sessions. It carries no case context: this run's own prompt shows up as cache_creation on that same turn, not as a read. So the RETRIEVAL measurement is clean; what is not comparable is the COST column.
cost.cost_comparability_note: Every sibling cross-repo graphify arm ran with prompt caching OFF (cache_read=0, paying full input price: $13.68-$24.30 per case). This run had caching ON, so its $3.73 is a cached price and must NOT be put in the same column as theirs. Re-run with DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1 if a like-for-like cost number is needed; the ranked answer does not change.
cost.cache_clean_note: cache_clean means no cache was inherited from an earlier session, which is what the run conditions require -- NOT that the run read no cache at all. In-run cache (the totals above) is expected and comparable. Judged on cache_read at the first assistant turn.
cost.surface_pure_note: Arm surface is Opus 5 with ONLY the graphify knowledge-graph MCP server (query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats, shortest_path) against a single merged graph. Bash/Read/Grep/Glob/Write/Edit and every other MCP server are excluded by --disallowedTools and --strict-mcp-config, so a filesystem-grep escape was not merely unused but impossible. Any tool outside the graphify allow-list counts as a surface violation.

sandbox.mechanism: sandbox-exec (macOS seatbelt), profile pinned at sandbox.sb
sandbox.gate4_verified_both_ways: before launch, run.sh proved golden.json UNREADABLE and the merged graph.json still READABLE under the same profile. Checking only the first is what let a stale path pass a tilde profile that denied nothing.
sandbox.note: The benchmark tree is denied wholesale and only the repo directories plus cross-repo/_indexes/graphify/merged and _indexes/graphify_mcp are re-allowed, so golden.json, DONOTREADTHISFOLDER/ and every sibling arm's results fail with EPERM. ~/.claude/projects is denied too, so no earlier session transcript - nor this run's own - is readable. cwd was a fresh empty directory, no settings sources were loaded and slash commands were disabled, so no CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins or hooks applied; auto-memory is unreadable under the sandbox.

cost.prompt_caching: default (in-run caching allowed by this case's run conditions)

index.build: per-repo `graphify extract <repo> --code-only --no-cluster`, then `graphify merge-graphs` into one cross-repo graph (shared across every cross-repo case, built once)
index.index_repo_gap_note: The run_prompt names 15 repositories; the merged graph contains nodes for only 14. `router` was never extracted (no _indexes/graphify/router directory, zero nodes with repo=router), so any router file in gold is unreachable on this surface. Recall is capped by the index, not by the model.
